answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may bid for work, then slash that stake when a randomly audited task shows duplicated control or fabricated results. An attacker cannot multiply influence merely by minting accounts: every sybil must tie up capital, and detected fraud destroys part of it. The nadir of trust is costly to recover from; even an ivory-colored reputation badge or mesa-sized account swarm cannot replace forfeited stake.
